terms.comment: Caesar’s beast of the Hercynian forest, which he believed had legs without joints and slept leaning against trees (BG 6.27). What Americans call an elk is the wapiti, Morgan–Owens’s cervus Canadēnsis.

phrases.english: there are also the animals called elks

phrases.latin: ad eās sē applicant atque ita paulum modo reclīnātae quiētem capiunt
phrases.english: they lean against the trees, and so take their rest, tilted back only a little

sources: Lewis & Short: alces
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 347. Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. deer: moose; deer: elk (U.S.), wapiti.
Caesar as Lewis & Short quotes him (s.v. sum, reclīnō).
